newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Westpac bid ruling weeks away - ACCC says.
newsitem.headline: Westpac bid ruling weeks away - ACCC says.

text.p: Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chairman Allan Fels said on Tuesday that the corporate regulator does not plan to make a ruling on Westpac Banking Corp's bid for Bank of Melbourne Ltd for at least a few weeks.
"It's a few weeks away," Fels told reporters at a conference in response to questions.
Westpac's bid values the regional bank at A$1.435 billion, or A$9.75 per share.
The ACCC has noted a number of times since the bid was launched on April 3 that regional banks played an important role in the economy of each state.

The Westpac bid would mean that the state of Victoria does not have a significant regional bank left, but the Sydney-based major has argued that it would not remove the Bank of Melbourne nametag entirely from the Victorian operations.
